extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in media outlets and online journalism
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia profile of a specific news and opinion website (Vox) describing its history, content strategy, formats, audience, and production choices. Useful for understanding how the site produces and positions news content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explainer / explanatory journalism mission
rubrics_metrics.description: The site seeks to explain news by providing additional contextual information not usually found in traditional news sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founding editors describe Vox's goal as making news understandable by adding context and background. This is central to editorial strategy and shapes story selection and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Card stacks for contextual definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Vox creates 'card stacks' in bright canary yellow that provide context and define terms within an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cards are perpetually maintained as a form of 'wiki page written by one person with a little attitude' and are reused across stories (example: a card about 'insurance exchange' reused for Affordable Care Act stories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia pairing: videos accompanied by articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Vox has a YouTube channel where videos are accompanied by an article on their website; the themes covered in the videos are usually similar to the themes covered in the regular, written articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Videos cover current affairs, timelines, and interesting facts. The YouTube channel complements written coverage and extends reach (noted subscriber/view counts and cross-platform partnerships such as the Netflix 'Explained' series).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technology / CMS to produce complex presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Vox uses Vox Media's Chorus content management system, which enables journalists to easily create articles with complex visual effects and transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include photos that change as the reader scrolls; technology is treated as a core part of making news more understandable and engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience targeting / demographic positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Vox Media's properties target educated households with six-figure incomes and a head of house less than 35 years old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This demographic targeting influences tone, subject matter, and presentation choices aimed at younger, relatively affluent readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing by topical expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The site's initial 20-person staff was chosen for their expertise in topic areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founders hired journalists with subject-matter competence (examples include hires from Slate and The Washington Post) to support explanatory, expert-driven coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast network and serialized audio formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Vox distributes numerous podcasts, all hosted by Vox staff, across a variety of formats and topical focuses (roundtable, interview, narrative) with regular schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The Weeds (twice-weekly roundtable on public policy), Worldly (foreign policy), Today, Explained (daily short explanations), Future Perfect (weekly on philanthropy/effective altruism), Unexplainable (weekly science panel), etc. Podcasts reinforce the explanatory mission in audio form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and original programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Vox has engaged in partnerships and original programming (e.g., a Netflix weekly TV show called Explained).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TV and streaming partnerships extend Vox's explanatory journalism into longer-form and visual formats, shaping production values and distribution strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial/ideological positioning and framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Vox has been described as left-leaning and liberal and is noted for framing news in ways that appeal to its young, liberal audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site has faced criticism for partisan commentary and for presenting analysis with an ideological slant; this positioning is part of how audiences and critics evaluate its output.
